notes: The clean Django case: a focused LTS-to-LTS upgrade, Django 3.2.25 -> 4.2.30 (both LTS; versions from requirements.txt, so the from/to is unambiguous). Only 5 files changed, 18/19 lines: requirements.txt, rorapi/settings.py, rorapi/common/urls.py, rorapi/v2/models.py and the .github/workflows/run_tests.yml CI file. Almost no unrelated churn, so ground truth is tight. MIT licensed, has a manage.py and a run_tests.yml CI workflow. Single parent (not a merge commit). Checks mirror what CI actually runs at base: services are MySQL 8.4 and Elasticsearch 7.10.0 (NOT Postgres); CI loads data with 'manage.py setup <TEST_DATA_DUMP_FILE> -t' then runs ONLY 'python manage.py test rorapi.tests.tests_unit' (the integration and functional suites are commented out in run_tests.yml with a 'TODO fix these' note, so a plain 'manage.py test' that runs everything does not match CI). TEST_DATA_DUMP_FILE and several secrets (AWS_REGION, LaunchDarkly) are CI-provided; confirm the dump file and MySQL/ES service setup before enabling L1 in M8.
